title: Codex Cloud adds reusable team environments; phone access was already here
summary: OpenAI's Codex Cloud DevDay update adds reusable development environments. Here is how publishing, task isolation, team access and prior phone support fit together.

# Codex Cloud adds reusable team environments; phone access was already here


By OpenTools Team


OpenAI's DevDay Codex update turns a tested repository setup into a published environment for separate cloud tasks. Teams need to check what that setup shares, and what still belongs to each task or user.


##


The new unit of reuse is the environment, not the task


[OpenAI's September 29 DevDay recap](https://openai.com/index/devday-2026-recap/) says Codex can now run in the cloud from any device using reusable development environments with team‑approved settings and permissions. For a team lead, the useful change is that repository setup can be prepared once and used to start separate cloud tasks. It is more specific than saying that Codex can be reached away from a laptop. OpenAI lists Plus, Pro, Business, Healthcare, Education and Enterprise availability for the Codex‑in‑the‑cloud announcement.


The linked[Codex Cloud guide](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cloud) describes an environment as the starting point for work: select repositories, let Codex install tools and dependencies, inspect its checks, save the configuration and publish it. Only after the environment is published does a new task start from that prepared setup. The[environment reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environments) says every task receives its own isolated workspace. In practical terms, two tasks can inherit the same approved toolchain without sharing a mutable working tree or each other's uncommitted edits.


##


A published setup and a running task change on different clocks


OpenAI's[saved‑state documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environments#reuse-and-update-saved-state) draws a line worth preserving during rollout. A newly started task uses the published environment's prepared filesystem; an existing task continues with its own saved files and installed tools. When the team changes the reusable setup, it edits and tests the environment, then republishes it for new work. Republishing is not described as silently replacing the state of tasks already underway. That distinction matters when a dependency or access policy changes: check the task's starting environment and its own later changes before assuming a republished template repaired it.


The same guide says Codex can[work on the web, mobile or desktop](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cloud) , with cloud tasks continuing while the user's computer sleeps. A published environment reduces repeated setup; it does not make every repository or external service automatically available. A team still has to review the repositories, installation steps, network destinations and credentials that the environment needs. The documented setup flow asks the owner to resolve missing access before publishing, which makes the environment itself an operational artifact to maintain, rather than a one‑time launch button.


##


Sharing a setup is not sharing a teammate's task


For Enterprise workspaces, OpenAI's[sharing instructions](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/environments/cloud-environments#share-an-environment-with-your-workspace) allow an environment owner to choose a workspace instead of Only me. The guide is explicit that access to the prepared setup does not confer access to somebody else's task or permission to edit the environment. It also separates repository access and personal connections by the account that runs the task. That is the important security boundary when a lead says an environment is "approved for the team": it describes a reusable starting configuration, not a blanket transfer of all project permissions or task history.


This is also not Codex's first remote‑access announcement. In[May, OpenAI added Codex to the ChatGPT mobile app](https://openai.com/index/work-with-codex-from-anywhere/) so a user could steer work running on a laptop, devbox or managed remote machine from a phone. The new DevDay story is the published cloud setup and separate hosted tasks, not the invention of phone control. OpenAI separately introduced[programmatic Agents API hosted sandboxes](https://openai.com/index/introducing-the-agents-api/) earlier in September; those serve developers building agent applications, while this Codex Cloud guide describes a user‑facing coding workflow. A team choosing between them should compare the operator, execution environment and integration surface, rather than treating every remote agent as the same product.


The[Codex tool record](https://opentools.ai/tools/codex) describes the broader coding agent, and its[OpenAI organization page](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) connects this launch to the maker. A reusable cloud environment is a feature of that tool, not a new LLM model or a separate product identity.
